title: How Costco Makes $9 Billion While Barely Profiting From Products
description_sources: Costco FY2026 Q4 and full-year results: https://investor.costco.com/news/news-details/2026/Costco-Wholesale-Corporation-Reports-Fourth-Quarter-and-Fiscal-Year-2026-Operating-Results/default.aspx

scenes.say: Last year, Costco sold almost three hundred billion dollars worth of stuff. And on all those products, it made almost nothing.
Yet the company still made over nine billion dollars in profit. So where does the money actually come from?
The answer is one of the smartest business models in the world. And once you see it, you'll spot it everywhere.

visual.title: How Costco Makes Money
visual.sub: the business model hiding in plain sight

scenes.say: The strange math.
Costco's total revenue last year was just over three hundred and three billion dollars. Almost all of that came from selling products.
Membership fees were only five point nine billion. That's less than two percent of revenue.

visual.title: Membership fees as a share of...

scenes.say: But here's the twist. Those same fees made up about half of Costco's operating profit.

visual.title: Membership fees as a share of...

scenes.say: In other words, Costco isn't really in the business of selling you groceries. It's in the business of selling you a membership card.
Why the products barely make money.
Costco reportedly caps its markup at fourteen percent on most brands, and fifteen percent on its own Kirkland brand. Many supermarkets mark items up far more.
After paying for staff, warehouses and shipping, Costco keeps only about two cents of operating profit for every dollar of products it sells.
That's why the famous one dollar fifty hot dog and soda combo hasn't changed price in decades. Cheap prices aren't a mistake. They're the marketing.

visual.sub: hot dog + soda · same price for decades

scenes.say: The membership machine.
Costco has about eighty-four million paid members. A basic membership in the US costs sixty-five dollars a year. Executive costs one hundred and thirty.

visual.title: Who pays Costco to shop there

scenes.say: Here's why this is so powerful. Membership fees are almost pure profit. There's no product to buy, no shelf to stock. And around nine in ten members renew every year.

visual.title: Why fees are the perfect revenue

scenes.say: That means Costco knows, a year in advance, where roughly half its operating profit will come from. Investors love that kind of predictability.

visual.title: Profit Costco can count on before the year starts

scenes.say: The flywheel.

Low prices attract more members. More members means Costco buys in enormous volume. Huge volume lets it squeeze suppliers for lower costs. And lower costs mean even lower prices. Then the loop starts again.
Costco also stocks only around four thousand items, while a typical supermarket carries tens of thousands. Fewer items means bigger orders of each one, and even better deals.
What this means for you.

First, as a shopper. The Executive membership gives two percent back on purchases. The upgrade costs sixty-five dollars more, so it only pays off if you spend over three thousand two hundred and fifty dollars a year.
Second, as an investor or a business builder. The best businesses often don't profit from what they sell. They profit from the relationship. Think Amazon Prime, Netflix, or your phone plan.
Costco gives away the products almost at cost, and charges you for the right to shop. That's the secret.
